messages:
alex_support: Hey team — customer_jones reports intermittent 502s hitting POST /v1/generate. They sent a request_id: 8f4a7d2e-cc9b-4f1a-9b2e-3a1b2c9d0e7f and says it happened ~2026-03-10 16:02:10 UTC. Can SRE check whether that req_id is still in hot logs or moved to archive? Also need guidance for a curl repro and what info to ask customer for.

customer_jones: adding the exact curl they used below so you have it: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-l1","input":"hello","max_tokens":10}'` — we also sent X-Request-ID header but not sure value was kept.

alex_support: thanks — they included it but not the X-Request-ID header value in the payload. they just pasted the command; the request_id above came from our client-side trace.

dana_sre: quick runbook: first search hot indices with a tight time window around 16:02 UTC. Hot retention is 30d; logs older than that may be in cold/archived storage (archived up to 365d, request required). If not in hot, we can raise an archive export (takes ~1-2h). :mag:

liam_engineer: KQL/Lucene snippet to run from Kibana (replace <REQID> and times):

```
request_id.keyword:"8f4a7d2e-cc9b-4f1a-9b2e-3a1b2c9d0e7f" OR trace.id:"8f4a7d2e-cc9b"
@timestamp:[2026-03-10T15:50:00.000Z TO 2026-03-10T16:10:00.000Z]
```

Also try a broader query if that misses: search for customer org/project id and 502s: `http.response.status_code:502 AND project_id:"acme-prod" AND @timestamp:[...range...]`. If nothing in hot, run archive_bot export: `archive_bot export --reqid 8f4a7d2e-... --range 2026-03-10T15:45:00Z/2026-03-10T16:15:00Z --reason "support_escalation"` (support will kick off).

liam_engineer: reproduction curl to send back to customer (ask them to run and include the exact X-Request-ID header):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 8f4a7d2e-cc9b-4f1a-9b2e-3a1b2c9d0e7f" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-l1","input":"smoke test for 502","max_tokens":8}'
```

Ask them to include exact response headers + full response body and the timestamp (client clock) when they saw the error.

alex_support: good. I'll ask for: exact curl with X-Request-ID, client timestamp, region they hit (us-west-2 / eu-west-1), project_id/org_id, and their SDK version. I'll also ask them to run the curl above and paste the response.

liam_engineer: if we find the request in hot logs, check these fields: `request_id`, `trace_id`, `upstream_status`, `pod`, `gpu_id`, `kv_cache_hit`, and `runtime.errors`. If we find a backend 500 that translated to 502, capture the stack traces and pod logs. If not in hot, file archive export and include the exact range — export ETA ~90-120m.

alex_support: noted. one more: what if the req_id is truncated in our logs? do we need to try partial matches?

dana_sre: yes — sometimes client-side UUIDs get truncated in proxy logs. Run a wildcard search on the first 8 chars: `request_id:*8f4a7d2e*` and also search `trace.id` and `span.id`. Also check `http.request.headers.x-request-id.keyword`.

liam_engineer: I'll start a quick hot index search now. If nothing, I'll escalate to archive_bot and post back with export ticket id. ETA for initial search 15m.

alex_support: great — I'll collect repro curl + timestamp from customer_jones and update thread. assigning to lia m for follow-up. :thumbsup:

archive_bot: archive-export-request-created id=AE-20260310-459 status=pending range=2026-03-10T15:45:00Z/2026-03-10T16:15:00Z submitted_by=liam_engineer link=https://internal.archive/AE-20260310-459

liam_engineer: update — found two entries in hot indices that look related (same trace id prefix). grabbing pod logs and attaching to export ticket. If customer can reproduce with the exact X-Request-ID, that'll help us correlate the rest.

alex_support: thanks — I'll push repro request to customer right now and ask them to upload any network captures. Will post back when they respond.

customer_jones: thanks -- running the repro now, will paste the full headers and response in ~5m.

liam_engineer: noted, holding on archive export until we confirm whether hot results are sufficient; will update AE ticket if we need deeper traces.

alex_support: closing loop for now — next actions: (1) collect repro curl + exact X-Request-ID + client timestamp + region from customer, (2) liam to share hot log hits / pod logs or archive ticket id, (3) support to follow up with timeline to customer.
